title: Assessing the concordance between an AI-Based Robotic Ultrasound System and Conventional Expert Ultrasound in Inflammatory and Structural Joint Assessment – the PIX-ROBO Study
summary:
Ultrasound has become an established diagnostic tool in rheumatology over recent decades. It allows clinicians to detect joint inflammation and structural damage without radiation exposure, at relatively low cost, and with the flexibility of repeated examinations. A significant limitation, however, is that result quality depends heavily on the operator's expertise, and trained specialists are not always readily available.
Robotic ultrasound systems combined with AI-based image analysis offer a promising approach to address this: by automating both image acquisition and interpretation, these systems have the potential to reduce dependence on individual expertise.
This multicenter study investigates whether such systems produce results comparable to those of conventional, specialist-performed ultrasound — with a particular focus on the assessment of joint inflammation (synovitis). The study includes adults with rheumatoid arthritis or psoriatic arthritis who have at least one actively inflamed joint.
All participants will be examined using both methods at study entry and again at 6, 12, and 24 months. These assessments are complemented by clinical evaluations of disease activity and X-rays of the hands and feet at the beginning and end of the study. Patient experiences with both examination methods will be captured through questionnaires.
The study aims to quantify the level of agreement between the two methods, compare the time required for each, and assess whether ultrasound findings can predict the progression of joint damage visible on X-ray.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) or psoriatic arthritis (PsA) according to the 2010 American College of Rheumatology (ACR)/ European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) or Classification Criteria for Psoriatic Arthritis (CASPAR) criteria respectively
- Willing and capable of giving informed consent, which must be obtained prior to any study-specific screening procedures 
 - Evidence of active arthritis, as shown by 1 or more clinically swollen joints among those scanned by ultrasound
- Willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, laboratory tests, and other study procedures 
- Willing and able to comply with the RUS system
Exclusion criteria:
- Unable to comprehend instructions necessary to perform the RUS examination
- Severe joint destruction, defined as previous amputation, joint surgery or deformation that prohibits the placing of hands on the examination table required for performing the RUS examination
